children: Shares of swimming pool distributor Pool

jumped 10.4% in the afternoon session after the company reported third-quarter net sales and adjusted earnings per share above analyst expectations and confirmed its annual adjusted diluted earnings per share guidance. According to the company’s press release, net sales rose 4% to $1.50 billion, accelerating from 2% growth in the second quarter and topping the $1.48 billion consensus. About 3 percentage points of that increase came from price, with the rest from stronger maintenance activity and building-materials growth. Chief Executive John Watwood said the company cut inventory 3% while growing sales through the end of the peak season, and returned $158.7 million to shareholders in the quarter through buybacks and dividends. The profit picture was less clean: gross margin fell 60 basis points to 29.0% on higher inbound freight, customer mix, and a tough comparison with last year’s mid-season price increases, and operating income declined 3% to $172.2 million. Adjusted earnings were $3.40 a share, a penny above a year ago and above the $3.36 consensus. Management confirmed full-year adjusted diluted earnings guidance of $10.87 to $11.17, a range whose midpoint sits slightly above the $10.99 consensus and excludes $0.21 a share of after-tax chief executive transition costs.
What is the market telling us

Pool’s shares are not very volatile and have only had 7 moves greater than 5% over the last year. Moves this big are rare for Pool and indicate this news significantly impacted the market’s perception of the business.

The biggest move we wrote about over the last year was 8 months ago when the stock dropped 13% on the news that it reported fourth-quarter 2025 earnings and revenue that missed analyst expectations and provided a weaker-than-anticipated forecast for 2026. Net sales for the quarter were flat year on year at $982.2 million, falling short of estimates. The company's profit also declined, with earnings per share (EPS) of $0.85, down from $0.98 in the same period the previous year and below forecasts. Looking ahead, the company guided for 2026 EPS with a midpoint of $11.00. This forecast also missed what analysts were expecting, signaling concerns about future profitability and modest growth.

Pool is down 17.6% since the beginning of the year, and at $189.17 per share, it is trading 37% below its 52-week high of $300.31 from October 2025. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of Pool’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at only $376.03.
